papers.title: The Optimal Sampler for Diverse TSP Solutions: Characterization, Limits, and Learning
papers.abstract: We address the Diverse Traveling Salesman Problem (D-TSP) that seeks a set of $k$ distinct TSP tours. Each selected tour must not exceed a prescribed multiple of the optimal tour length, while the maximum pairwise Jaccard similarity within the selected set is minimized. This formulation is important for applications requiring both solution quality and fault tolerance, such as logistics planning, robotics, and strategic patrolling. We propose a novel hybrid framework that decomposes D-TSP into a sampling stage and a selection stage. The selection stage is a max-min dispersion problem, for which any approximation better than a factor of two is NP-hard; we therefore focus on the sampling stage. Our contributions are both theoretical and empirical. Theoretically, we give two end-to-end guarantees for the optimal sampling distribution, from two perspectives: including an optimal set in the sampled pool, or having at least $k$ mutually distant tours in the pool. The second reduces the number of samples from exponential to linear in $k$, at the cost of weakening the benchmark from the best $k$ tours to the best $\beta k$ for some $\beta > 1$. For practical use, we prove that a pipeline that samples spanning trees and then converts to tours does not hurt the quality of the pool in principle. Empirically, both objectives are learnable, and our experiments not only validate the analysis but also outperform the baselines on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, by a single trained model with no fine-tuning.

papers.title: Pinch-Free Orientations of Polyomino Grid Graphs
papers.abstract: We study lattice-based collective construction of a target polyomino on the integer grid, where robots place unit square blocks subject to two physical constraints: the partial structure must remain connected at all times, and no placement may create an unfillable one-cell gap. We present a wavefront sweep algorithm that computes a dependency structure satisfying the local conditions required for safe assembly. Given a list of n cells sorted lexicographically by coordinates, the orientation can be computed in O(n) time using O(n) auxiliary space.

papers.title: How to Walk a Dog in Parallel: On Parallel Computation of the Discrete Frechet Distance
papers.abstract: The Fr\'echet distance (also known as the dog-leash distance) is a well-studied and prevalent distance measure for polygonal curves. In this paper we present parallel algorithms for computing the discrete \frechet\ distance between two curves, in both the PRAM and MPC models. For two polygonal curves of length $n$, we show that the distance between them can be computed in the PRAM model in $O(\log n/ \sigma)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{2+\sigma})$ total work for any $0<\sigma<1$. In the sublinear MPC model with $n^\rho$ space per machine, it can be computed in $O(\log n / \rho^2)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{2+\rho})$ total space. For $c$-packed curves, we match our bounds to the sequential algorithms, showing that a $(1+\eps)$-approximation of the distance can be computed in the PRAM model in $O(\log{n}+1/\sigma^3)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{1+\sigma})$ total work, and in the sublinear MPC model in $O(1 /\rho^3)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{1+\rho})$ total space, for any constant $\eps>0$. As part of our algorithms for $c$-packed curves, we also present parallel algorithms for computing curve simplifications, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: The Stretch Factor of Planar Delaunay Triangulations Is Less Than 1.5949
papers.abstract: Delaunay triangulations are the classical plane spanners: the shortest path between two vertices is at most a constant times as long as the segment between them. Determining the smallest such constant, the worst-case stretch factor of Delaunay triangulations, is a long-standing open problem; the best known lower and upper bounds were 1.5932, due to Xia and Zhang, and 1.998, due to Xia. We focus on the upper bound. Xia's analysis replaces the triangulation by a chain of disks and compares the length along the whole chain with the straight-line distance at once, by induction with a potential function. We propose a new framework, progress accounting, which compares the contribution of each single disk to the chain length with the progress of that disk along the straight line. This turns the global analysis into a local one, which can be made very precise. The key to the local analysis is our pencil lemma: it shows that the comparison for each disk needs only four angles, whatever the rest of the chain looks like. The resulting conditions on one function of four angles are verified by a computer-assisted proof in exact rational and interval arithmetic; corner lemmas handle the degenerate configurations where the conditions are tight. As a result, every Delaunay triangulation of a finite planar point set has stretch factor less than 1.5949. The gap to the best known lower bound shrinks from about 0.405 to less than 0.0017, by a factor of more than 200. This also shows that every finite planar point set has a plane spanner with stretch factor less than 1.5949, improving the previous bound of 1.998.

papers.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a strictly convex body and let $Z\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of sites in general position. We consider the problem of calculating the volume $\mu_d$ of $\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K)$. Let $V_z$ be the Voronoi cell of $z\in Z$ with respect to the convex distance function induced by $K$, and let $N$ be the nerve of the Voronoi cells. When $K$ is a ball, a classical result reduces the inclusion-exclusion formula to a sum over $N$: $\mu_d(\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K))=\sum_{J\in N}(-1)^{|J|+1}\mu_d(\bigcap_{z\in J}(z-K))$. When may the hypothesis that $K$ is a ball be dropped? We show that for $d\leq 2$ the reduced formula holds for every strictly convex $K$, while for each $d\geq 3$ there is a strictly convex $K$ for which it fails. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\chi_x$ be the Euler characteristic of the subcomplex of $N$ induced by the sites lying in $K+x$. A sufficient condition for the reduced formula to hold is $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union. When $d=3$ and $K$ is $C^4$, we show that $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union for all $Z$ in general position if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid. The proof relies on the Fubini-Pick affine invariant.
